findings.description: The calculation `(max + 1) * sizeof(int)` in `malloc` can overflow if `max` is very large, leading to a buffer smaller than intended.
If `malloc` fails (returns `NULL`), the code does not check and will dereference a `NULL` pointer, leading to undefined behavior or crash.
If the input array contains negative numbers or values greater than `max`, `count[arr[i]]++` and similar lines will access out-of-bounds memory.
If `max` is negative (e.g., all elements are negative), `(max + 1)` will be zero or negative, leading to undefined behavior in `malloc`.
The function assumes `n > 0` and `arr` is not `NULL`.
